_README: THIS IS A SECURITY DECLARATION, NOT CONFIGURATION.
An entry here states that a function is DELIBERATELY reachable without the gateway JWT check,
and that it does its own authentication. Adding one expands the public attack surface.
Review a diff to this file as a security decision, not a config tweak.
Modes: hmac = verifies a signature itself. platform-api-key = checks a platform key header.
orbi-api-key = checks against orbi_api_keys table (SHA-256 hash, revoked_at IS NULL).
none = intentionally public, no auth at all.
internal-worker-token = checks X-Internal-Worker-Token header against a vault secret (service-internal callers only, never exposed to integrators).

widget-token = authenticates with a widget_token in the request BODY only, no headers. The token is a pending_widget_sessions row id, minted server-to-server by or-link-mint-token; the platform and app_user_id are read off that row and can never be named by the caller. It is a short-lived bearer credential (300s default, 900s max), validated WITHOUT being consumed unless the function is the designated burn site (or-link-complete / or-quiltt-link-complete), so its replay window is the remaining TTL rather than a single request. It exists because a host app's user has no OrangeRails JWT and a browser must never hold a platform key.

platform-api-key-or-widget-token = accepts a platform key header, OR a widget_token in the request BODY when no key header is present. Same widget_token as the widget-token mode above. See authenticateWidgetToken in _shared/platform-auth.ts.
A NOTE ON platform-api-key: authenticateRequest in _shared/platform-auth.ts resolves EITHER an
X-Platform-API-Key header OR a Supabase JWT (direct mode). So any entry below labelled
platform-api-key (alone or combined with widget-token) accepts a direct JWT too, UNLESS the
function itself checks ctx.mode and refuses anything but platform mode. Six functions do that
check and are exactly right as labelled: or-link-mint-token, or-quiltt-session,
or-quiltt-accounts, or-quiltt-disconnect, or-sync-key-register, and or-platform-bootstrap
(which does its own key check and never accepts a JWT at all). Every other platform-api-key
entry is really "platform key or Supabase JWT"; this note stands in for a dedicated mode name
so the file does not need one added per entry.
CI (scripts/check-public-auth.mjs) asserts this file and config.toml agree in both directions.
It checks function NAMES only, never that the declared mode matches the implementation -- that
part is a human read, same as any other security decision.
